title: Hosted API - embeddings & rerank demo
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood. Omar and Tess are with me, we'll run through embeddings + rerank on the hosted API and show the console.
[00:12] Lena Park: Hi, thanks, excited. quick context, we're migrating from in-house vector store and looking to improve relevance for product search across mobile and web.
[00:23] Omar Rahman: Great. curious about latency and cost SLOs up front?
[00:29] Devon Ortiz: Latency goal is sub 120ms 95p for query path; cost target is we can't exceed our current per-query budget by more than 30%.
[00:40] Maya: Perfect, we'll show how embeddings + rerank can be tuned to hit that. quick agenda: demo API flow, console observability, then Optimize recommendations.
[00:52] Tess Alvarez: Note we often show two patterns: precompute embeddings + ANN store for candidate retrieval, then server-side rerank with a small cross-encoder model via hosted rerank endpoint.
[01:10] Priya Nair: Are those hosted as two separate endpoints? how are they priced?
[01:16] Maya: Yes. embeddings endpoint per embedding unit, rerank is generate-like pricing per token; we'll send the pricing sheet after.
[01:26] Omar: Also Optimize suggests batching and model family choices to hit latency/cost targets automatically.
[01:34] [02:05] Tess: (screen share) starting with code; here's a simple embedding call to REDWOOD_HOSTED/v1/embeddings body: text list etc.
[02:24] Devon: so we just push vectors to our vector DB?
[02:28] Tess: Exactly — precompute offline, store in your ANN, we recommend HNSW or FAISS. retrieval then returns top-k candidates.
[02:40] [03:05] Omar: Now rerank, we call the hosted rerank endpoint with the query and top-k docs, you can choose cross-encoder or lightweight semantic score.
[03:20] Samir Gupta: Are there limits on input size for rerank? we have long product descriptions.
[03:27] Maya: For hosted rerank we support chunking strategies, and the console shows per-request token breakdown; for really long docs we recommend prefixing with the most relevant snippet.
[03:40] Priya: How does caching work? we have a lot of repeated queries.
[03:44] Omar: Redwood has automatic prefix/KV cache for the model runtime; caching helps reduce repeated token compute. full details in Optimize suggestions.
[03:58] [05:02] Tess: Switching to console — here's the per-route latency graph, token cost heatmap. you can set alerts if cost spike or quality regression on eval sets.
[05:20] Lena: Can we map this to our A/B experiment ids? we want to correlate changes in relevance with user metrics.
[05:28] Maya: Yep the console supports metadata tagging per-request and you can instrument user ids/experiment ids, then filter traces.
[05:35] Devon: what about security, VPC, and data residency? some of our customers need EU-only.
[05:41] Omar: Hosted transitively supports region pinning, and for strict residency you can use Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated. both support customer KMS integration.
[05:52] Priya: Do you have SOC2 or ISO certs?
[05:55] Maya: We are SOC 2 Type II in 2025, and have ISO27001 in progress; I'll attach the security pack.
[06:05] [07:00] Tess: Back to rerank accuracy — here's an example of before/after using a cross-encoder reranker on a sample query. notice improved MRR and fewer poor top-3 results.
[07:20] Devon: Any idea of throughput? our peak is around 700 qps across regions.
[07:27] Omar: For that scale we recommend Dedicated or autoscale Dedicated pools; hosted can do spikes but with some constraints depending on concurrency — Optimize can suggest batching policy and whether quantized models would meet latency.
[07:45] Lena: If we go Dedicated, how is rollback handled on model changes?
[07:50] Maya: Console supports rollouts/canaries and automatic fallback to previous model variants.
[07:56] [09:10] Priya: Regarding embeddings dimensionality — what's recommended?
[09:15] Tess: Usually 1536 or 1024 depending on model family; Optimize can recommend dimensionality and quantization for your workload.
[09:27] Samir: Competitors we've looked at include Pinecone and OpenSearch. any differentiators?
[09:33] Omar: We focus on inference economics and unified tooling: same API for hosted, dedicated, private, plus rerank endpoint and console observability.
[09:44] [10:30] Maya: Quick live test — I'll run a sample query through embedding + ANN + rerank.
[10:37] [10:40] Maya: typing... (demo shows request/response) you can see token breakdown: embedding call ~0.9ms server-side + ANN lookup 12ms + rerank 80ms.
[10:58] Devon: that's promising, fits our 120ms goal in this example.
[11:05] Tess: note this is small cross-encoder; larger rerank models add latency but improve relevance.
[11:13] Priya: Could we run our test set to get regression numbers?
[11:17] Maya: yes, we can run benchmark against your eval set, and we'll instrument trace ids.
[11:25] [12:00] Omar: A quick note about integration: you can host ANN in any vendor, and Redwood's SDKs include helpers for backfilling and batch embedding pipelines.
[12:12] Lena: What about cost predictability? our finance team wants monthly forecasts.
[12:18] Maya: Dedicated gives predictable throughput pricing; hosted has usage rates but Optimize can produce forecasts from past usage patterns; we'll share the forecast template.
[12:30] [14:20] Devon: A potential blocker: some legal folks ask for on-prem air-gapped option.
[14:25] Omar: That's Redwood Private on-prem packaging; it includes customer-managed control plane and HSM/KMS.
[14:33] Priya: Are logs stored? how long?
[14:36] Maya: By default we retain logs for 30 days on hosted; enterprise retention is configurable as an add-on. audit logs and export available for Private.
[14:50] [16:00] Tess: back to Optimize — here's automatic batching suggestions, model family tradeoffs and quantization levels. you can apply suggestions per-route.
[16:18] Lena: How intrusive are quantization changes to relevance?
[16:22] Omar: Quantization reduces size/latency but can slightly shift semantics; Optimize runs evals to surface expected quality delta.
[16:34] [18:00] Maya: Questions?
[18:03] Priya: For the rerank endpoint, can we pass in custom features (click signals) with docs?
[18:09] Tess: Yes you can pass auxiliary features; reranker can incorporate scores or click features as structured inputs.
[18:19] Devon: Any built-in monitoring for concept drift?
[18:23] Omar: We have quality monitoring tied to prompt sets/eval results and can alert on regression.
[18:31] [20:05] Maya: Recap: embedding + ANN + rerank pattern recommended, console observability and Optimize for cost/latency tradeoffs, several deployment options for security/residency.
[20:18] Lena: Next steps from our side: share eval set and scope pilot, legal will request security pack.
[20:27] Maya: Great. we'll send pricing, security docs, and a pilot proposal.
[20:35] [21:15] Priya: small nit — can the rerank endpoint do partial rerank for top-10 only?
[21:21] Omar: yes you choose top-k to send; partial rerank is common.
[21:29] Samir: timeline — we'd like a 6 week pilot starting mid April.
[21:34] Maya: That should be doable, depends on legal.
[21:40] [22:50] Tess: I'll note recommended models and a sample config for batching.
[22:58] Devon: ok thanks.
[23:05] Maya: I'll follow up with action items. thanks everyone.
[23:12] [END]
summary: Demo of Redwood hosted embeddings + rerank pattern for StellarSearch. Showed embedding + ANN retrieval then hosted rerank endpoint; console observability and Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization. Discussed latency targets (~120ms), Dedicated vs Hosted for throughput, security options (VPC/Private, KMS, SOC2), and next steps: pilot, share security pack, pricing.
